question.problem: Given that $X∼B(7,0.9),$ compute $P(X<6).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(7,0.9),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x})(0.9)^{x}(0.1)^{7-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X<6)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,…,5.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X\ge 6)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=6,7,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X\ge 6),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =P(X\in \{6,7\}) \\  & =f(6)+f(7) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{6})(0.9)^{6}(0.1)^{7-6}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{7})(0.9)^{7}(0.1)^{7-7} \\  & =7(0.9)^{6}(0.1)+(0.9)^{7} \\  & ≈0.8503\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<6) & =1-P(X\ge 6) \\  & ≈1-0.8503 \\  & =0.1497\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.
